title: Translating Natural Language Arguments to Computational Arguments Using LLMs
authors: Gustavo Trajano; Daniel C. Engelmann; Rafael H. Bordini; S. Sarkadi; Jack Mumford; Alison R. Panisson
task_description: Classify a natural-language argument using argumentation schemes, retrieve/provide scheme descriptions and examples as context, and translate the argument into a computational representation.
inputs: Natural-language arguments; scheme labels; retrieved scheme descriptions/examples
outputs_or_labels: Computational argument representation; translation quality; context-size comparison
pipeline_gap_filled: Argument-form classification -> context provision/RAG -> structured argument output
artifact_access_status: paper_and_pdf_accessible; artifact identity not separately verified
evidence_basis: Liverpool repository abstract and published PDF record; DOI 10.3233/FAIA240329
limitations: Does not establish a separately released benchmark dataset; evaluation scope and reusable artifact status are unclear; context is scheme/example provision rather than proof-minimal compression.
why_relevant: Closest located precedent: scheme labels directly condition the context/examples supplied to an LLM, and the paper reports short-versus-larger context behavior plus wrong-scheme retrieval concerns in the inspected evidence.

title: Verification and Refinement of Natural Language Explanations through LLM-Symbolic Theorem Proving
authors: Xin Quan; Marco Valentino; Louise A. Dennis; Andre Freitas
task_description: Generate and formalize explanatory sentences, identify sufficient/necessary and relevant/redundant/unrelated facts, construct a formal theory, and verify/refine the resulting proof with a theorem prover.
inputs: NLI problems; natural-language explanations; candidate explanatory facts/sentences
outputs_or_labels: Selected facts/axioms; inference strategy; theorem-prover validity and refinement feedback
pipeline_gap_filled: Context selection/compression -> formal proof context -> verified reasoning
evidence_basis: ACL landing page and PDF; paper states released data link and neuro-symbolic framework
limitations: No Walton-style or cross-tradition argument-form classification; selection is NLI explanation/proof oriented rather than argument-scheme conditioned.
why_relevant: Strongest proof-relevant context-construction benchmark precedent, useful as a downstream selection/faithfulness comparator even though the form-classification stage is absent.

title: FRVA: Fact-Retrieval and Verification Augmented Entailment Tree Generation for Explainable Question Answering
task_description: Retrieve and filter irrelevant facts, then generate and verify deductive/abductive entailment trees with cross-verification.
outputs_or_labels: Filtered facts; entailment trees; fact-selection and structural-correctness scores
pipeline_gap_filled: Proof-relevant context selection -> explicit reasoning skeleton -> verified output
evidence_basis: ACL paper landing page and retained local summary
limitations: Inputs are already fact statements and entailment-tree data; no argument-form/scheme classifier; controlled domain and alternative valid trees complicate evaluation.
why_relevant: Provides a benchmarkable intervention for selecting proof-relevant context before structured reasoning, a key comparator for any form-conditioned selector.

title: Mining Complex Patterns of Argumentative Reasoning in Natural Language Dialogue
authors: Ramon Ruiz-Dolz; Zlata Kikteva; John Lawrence
task_description: Mine argumentation schemes in natural-language dialogue and evaluate Transformer/LLM classification, including transfer from textbook-like schemes to political debate.
inputs: Extracted dialogue arguments; textbook-like scheme corpus; political debate
outputs_or_labels: 441 arguments annotated with 24 scheme labels; scheme-family labels; classification scores
pipeline_gap_filled: Argument-form classification benchmark only; no context selection/compression stage
evidence_basis: ACL paper abstract and local retained summary
limitations: Small effective annotated set; class imbalance; annotation cost; no predicted-scheme-conditioned retrieval or downstream proof/context evaluation.
why_relevant: Best current fine-grained scheme-label benchmark for supplying the classification side of a future combined benchmark; should be paired with a selector/compressor intervention.

title: EthiX: A Dataset for Argument Scheme Classification in Ethical Debates
authors: Elfia Bezou-Vrakatseli; Oana Cocarascu; Sanjay Modgil
task_description: Classify human-authored ethical-debate arguments into Walton-based argument-scheme classes and test generalization across topics.
inputs: 686 curated Kialo arguments across 22 ethical topics
outputs_or_labels: Eight Walton-based scheme labels; topic-generalization results
pipeline_gap_filled: Argument-form classification benchmark only; no retrieval/compression objective
evidence_basis: SAGE/FAIA paper record and local retained summary
limitations: No context-budget manipulation, retrieval policy, compression faithfulness, or downstream reasoning evaluation.
why_relevant: Useful naturalistic and topical benchmark for the form-label input to a combined form-conditioned selection study.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
authors: Fangyuan Xu; Weijia Shi; Eunsol Choi
task_description: Train extractive and abstractive compressors to select/summarize retrieved documents for downstream LM performance; allow empty context when retrieval adds no value.
inputs: Retrieved documents; downstream LM queries; open-domain QA and language-modeling tasks
outputs_or_labels: Selected sentences or summaries; empty-context decisions; end-task performance and compression rate
pipeline_gap_filled: Context selection/compression benchmark only; no argument-form labels
evidence_basis: ICLR paper/PDF, arXiv record, and official code README
limitations: No argument mining, scheme labels, proof dependencies, or structured argument outputs; generic QA/language-modeling regime.
why_relevant: Strong baseline for selective augmentation and compression metrics that can be reused after adding argument-form-conditioned selection.

title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
task_description: Treat prompt compression as token classification learned by distillation, and evaluate faithfulness, compression, speed, and downstream task performance.
inputs: Prompts from MeetingBank, LongBench, ZeroScrolls, GSM8K, BBH
outputs_or_labels: Token keep/drop labels; compressed prompts; compression ratios; downstream scores
pipeline_gap_filled: Token-level context compression benchmark only; no argument-form conditioning
evidence_basis: ACL paper/PDF and official Microsoft code link
limitations: Token-level pruning does not preserve explicit argument roles, scheme labels, proof dependencies, or provenance; task-agnostic setup.
why_relevant: Provides a reproducible compression control and faithfulness/speed evaluation template for a form-conditioned selector.

title: LeanDojo: Theorem Proving with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
task_description: Extract proof data and premise-use annotations, retrieve relevant premises from a large formal library, and condition an LM-based prover on the selected premises.
inputs: Lean proof states; Mathlib premises; theorem/proof trajectories
outputs_or_labels: Premise-use annotations; retrieved premises; proof success
pipeline_gap_filled: Proof-relevant context selection -> LM proving, but formal premise selection is not natural-language argument-form classification
evidence_basis: NeurIPS/arXiv record and local premise-selection summary
limitations: Formal-only setting; no Walton/Toulmin/dialogue scheme labels; proof-state similarity/accessibility rather than cross-tradition form conditioning.
why_relevant: Closest mature retrieval-augmented proof benchmark for testing whether adding explicit form labels improves premise recall and proof success.
